state: Can tests must allow arbitrary ordinary Can functions and keep test scenarios, expected values, retries, selection and verdicts in Can. Authors are AI coding agents, favoring explicit typed contracts and precise diagnostics. The selected design uses a qualified reference toolchain R to compile the judge to TypeScript/Bun, candidate C as subject, and independent Go owner N for resources and cleanup. Accepted R/N executables and compiled suite ingress do not yet exist. Four bounded mechanics probes used temporary Python/POSIX supervision and native TypeScript instruments. PM-N1 preserved hostile then-getter object identity through inert numeric handles; an explicit read counted once and deliberate Promise assimilation broke the zero-read control. PM-N2 invoked actual runtime/codec/json.ts::encodeJSON: [1n] encoded as [1]; an accessor-backed array was rejected without reading the getter; an eager-read shim was detected. This bypassed generated Can/createCodec and proves no compiled Can ingress or R oracle. PM-F1 kept binary fd 0 separate from UTF-8 fd 3, distinguished empty from absent, caught withheld EOF and malformed snapshots, and stopped a nonreader writer after child exit; Python/POSIX is not Go ExtraFiles or product-launcher qualification. PM-B1 delivered route tokens and ping while an actual Playwright click remained pending; an external parent resolved it and saw the marker. Serialization behind the click deadlocked as intended. Aborting the route during close could fulfill the click, so click settlement and delivered result must be observed separately. A corrected control preserved both facts. Nevertheless Chrome triggered unexpected macOS Keychain UI. Parent-owned headless Chrome used temporary HOME/profile and loopback CDP, but omitted --password-store=basic and --use-mock-keychain present in pinned Playwright defaults. This is plausible causation, not exact process attribution. User canceled the dialog. All owned children and scratch are gone. Overall B1 remains failed despite protocol support. No more browser runs are requested. Future browser admission needs explicit noninteractive credentials, qualified absence of host UI, and cleanup independent of case/driver death. Observed browser peak was 1.72 GiB and 15 processes, from sampling, not strict quotas. Existing quick policy caps are 4 GiB, 64 processes, 512 MiB scratch, one live case/browser context; strict enforcement is required but not qualified on this MacBook with 256 GB disk. Broad builds and performance measurements are deferred. No coverage was migrated and all integrated N1/N2/B1/F1 gates remain unrun. This review must fix interfaces before dependency-ordered implementation planning, without claiming acceptance.

browser_launch.instructions: Which browser-launch contract should be the first implementation candidate, given the host UI failure and external ownership requirement?

criteria.driver_launch: Use pinned Playwright launch inside an N-owned resource service with pre-effect registration; preserve its test credential defaults, record effective configuration, and qualify host isolation plus service-death cleanup before admission.
criteria.direct_launch: Keep N spawning Chrome directly with a complete versioned launch recipe audited against pinned driver defaults, then qualify credential isolation and descendant cleanup independently.
criteria.isolated_host: Require a separately provisioned isolated browser execution host before implementing browser cases, retaining the same Can operations and trust receipts.

bridge_order.instructions: How should the remaining compiled Can ingress uncertainty constrain the upcoming implementation plan?

criteria.gated_lane: Allow the plan now, placing a minimal materialized C/typed same-realm ingress and R/N qualification lane before any dependent native migration; failed acceptance reopens the bridge design.
criteria.probe_first: Require an additional compiled-Can feasibility experiment before writing any implementation lanes, including the minimal compiler/entry/owner work it needs.
criteria.interpreter_first: Reopen the full interpreter architecture before scheduling the remaining native bridge work.
